CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: Not applicable (prenatal)
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Prenatal testing via amniocentesis at 13 weeks gestation
Clinical Indication: Screening for Down syndrome (trisomy 21) and other chromosomal abnormalities
Previous Testing: Rapid PCR analysis performed (see below)

TEST PERFORMED
G-banded Chromosome Analysis (Karyotype)

METHODOLOGY
Amniotic fluid cells were cultured using standard in situ culture techniques. Metaphase chromosomes were harvested and G-banded using trypsin-Giemsa staining. A minimum of 20 metaphase cells were analyzed at the 400-550 band level of resolution. Five cells were fully karyotyped and documented.

RESULTS
Karyotype: 46,XY

INTERPRETATION
Male chromosome complement with normal karyotype 46,XY. No evidence of trisomy 21 or other chromosomal abnormalities detected. All chromosomes appear structurally normal with no evidence of deletions, duplications, or rearrangements at the resolution of this analysis.

This result supersedes the previous rapid PCR analysis performed on this specimen.

QUALITY ASSURANCE
Number of colonies analyzed: 4
Number of cells counted: 20
Number of cells analyzed: 20
Number of cells karyotyped: 5
Band resolution: 400-550 bands

LIMITATIONS
This test can detect numerical chromosome abnormalities and structural rearrangements larger than 5-10 Mb. Smaller deletions, duplications, or rearrangements below the resolution of conventional cytogenetics may not be detected. This test does not detect single gene disorders, uniparental disomy, or low-level mosaicism (<10%).

RECOMMENDATIONS
The karyotype analysis shows a normal male chromosome complement. This result supersedes previous rapid PCR analysis. No additional cytogenetic testing is indicated based on these findings. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these results in the context of the pregnancy.
